title: Essential Hypertension: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACC/AHA & JAMA)
snippet: Meta-analysis confirms lowering SBP by 10 mmHg reduces major cardiovascular events by 20%, stroke by 27%, and heart failure by 28%. First-line pharmacological classes (thiazide diuretics, CCBs, ACEi/ARBs) demonstrate equivalent mortality reduction; CCBs excel in stroke prevention (RR 0.82), while ACEi/ARBs offer superior renal protection in diabetic cohorts (HR 0.68). Guideline Protocol: DASH diet adherence (approx. 11 mmHg SBP reduction in hypertensive adults); dietary sodium restriction to <1,500 mg/day (or at least 1,000 mg/day reduction); aerobic exercise 90-150 min/week; potassium supplementation (3,500-5,000 mg/day via diet unless CKD present). Thresholds: Stage 1: 130-139 / 80-89 mmHg (lifestyle modification + 10-year ASCVD risk stratification); Stage 2: ≥140/90 mmHg (lifestyle + combination guideline therapy).

title: Hypercholesterolemia & Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AHA/ACC/Multisociety)
snippet: Extensive meta-analyses of Cholesterol Treatment Trialists (CTT) show a 21% reduction in major vascular events per 1.0 mmol/L (~39 mg/dL) reduction in LDL-C. High-intensity statin therapy reduces LDL-C by ≥50%, moderate-intensity by 30-49%. Addition of non-statins (Ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors) yields proportional additional cardiovascular event risk reductions. Guideline Protocol: Mediterranean or plant-forward dietary pattern: saturated fat <7% of total calories; elimination of trans fats; 25-30 g/day dietary fiber (7-13 g soluble fiber). Thresholds: Primary prevention: 10-year ASCVD risk threshold ≥7.5% warrants statin discussion; secondary prevention: target LDL-C <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L) in very high-risk individuals.

title: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) & Pulmonary Embolism (PE): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (CHEST)
snippet: CHEST guidelines strongly recommend DOACs (Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, Dabigatran, Edoxaban) over Vitamin K antagonists for initial and long-term VTE management in non-cancer patients (Grade 1B). title: Stable Ischemic Heart Disease & Angina: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (ISCHEMIA))
snippet: In 5,179 patients with moderate or severe ischemia, an initial invasive strategy (angiography and revascularization plus medical therapy) did not reduce major ischemic cardiovascular events or all-cause death compared to an initial conservative strategy of optimal medical therapy alone (cumulative 5-year event rate 13.3% vs. 15.5%; p=0.34). Guideline Protocol: Supervised exercise training (30-60 min of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise 5+ days/week); smoking cessation (absolute risk reduction of CV events >30%); stress management protocols. Thresholds: Revascularization reserved for failure of optimal medical therapy to control symptoms or left main stem/high-risk anatomy.

title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH / NASH): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (MAESTRO-NASH))
snippet: In 966 patients with biopsy-proven MASH and fibrosis stages F1B-F3, Resmetirom (thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist) achieved MASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis in 29.9% (100 mg) vs. 9.7% (placebo) (p<0.001), and fibrosis improvement of at least one stage with no worsening of NAFLD activity score in 25.9% vs. 14.2% (p<0.001). title: Primary Hypothyroidism: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ATA / AACE)
snippet: Guidelines establish Levothyroxine monotherapy as standard of care. Full replacement dose is approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day in healthy adults, with lower initiation doses (25-50 mcg) in elderly patients or those with coronary artery disease to avoid precipitating cardiac ischemia. Routine addition of Liothyronine (T3) is not recommended by consensus due to lack of sustained RCT benefit. Guideline Protocol: Strict administration timing: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water 30-60 minutes before breakfast, or at bedtime (3-4 hours after the last meal); separate by ≥4 hours from calcium, iron, or antacids. Thresholds: Target TSH range: 0.5-4.5 mIU/L (adjusted to 4.0-7.0 mIU/L in elderly adults >70-80 years to prevent overreplacement osteopenia/AFib).

title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ESHRE / ASRM / Monash)
snippet: Diagnosis confirmed via Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3: oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound). title: Adult Persistent Asthma: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (GINA)
snippet: GINA Track 1 establishes low-dose ICS-Formoterol as the preferred reliever across all asthma severities. SYGMA 1 and 2 trials (NEJM 2018) proved as-needed ICS-Formoterol reduces severe exacerbations by 60-64% compared to SABA-only therapy, while reducing steroid exposure by 75-83%. Guideline Protocol: Identification and mitigation of environmental triggers (tobacco smoke, indoor dust mites, animal dander, mold); written personalized Asthma Action Plan; inhaler technique demonstration at every clinical visit. Thresholds: Step-up or step-down evaluation based on symptom control validated questionnaires (e.g., Asthma Control Test [ACT] score ≥20 indicates control).

title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ATS / IDSA)
snippet: Clinical guideline establishes CURB-65 or Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) to determine outpatient vs. inpatient site of care. For healthy outpatients without comorbidities, monotherapy with Amoxicillin (1 g TID) or Doxycycline is strongly recommended over macrolides due to widespread pneumococcal resistance. title: Knee & Hip Osteoarthritis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (OARSI & ACR)

title: Gout & Hyperuricemia: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACR)
snippet: Strong recommendation for a Treat-to-Target urate-lowering strategy. Allopurinol is the preferred first-line xanthine oxidase inhibitor. title: Chronic Non-Specific Lower Back Pain: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACP & The Lancet Series)
snippet: ACP guidelines recommend that clinicians and patients initially select nonpharmacological treatment with exercise, multidisciplinary rehabilitation, acupuncture, mindfulness-based stress reduction, or spinal manipulation (Grade: strong recommendation). title: Postmenopausal Osteoporosis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Endocrine Society)
snippet: Guidelines recommend initial treatment with oral bisphosphonates (Alendronate, Risedronate) or IV Zoledronic acid for postmenopausal women at high risk of fractures, reducing vertebral fractures by ~50-70% and hip fractures by ~40% (FIT and HORIZON trials). title: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAD)
snippet: AAD guidelines emphasize basic barrier repair with bland emollient ointments as foundational therapy. Topical corticosteroids (TCS) are first-line prescription therapy for flares. Topical calcineurin inhibitors (Tacrolimus) and PDE-4 inhibitors (Crisaborole) are recommended for sensitive areas (face, neck, skin folds). For moderate-to-severe disease refractory to topicals, biologic therapy with Dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα; LIBERTY AD trials, NEJM) provides significant clearance with an excellent safety profile. Guideline Protocol: 'Soak and Seal' routine: Daily lukewarm baths/showers (5-10 minutes) followed immediately within 3 minutes by liberal application of thick petrolatum- or ceramide-based ointments; use of gentle, fragrance-free cleansers; wearing loose 100% cotton clothing. Thresholds: Assess disease severity using validated tools like EASI (Eczema Area and Severity Index) or SCORAD.

title: Plaque Psoriasis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAD / NPF)
snippet: For localized disease (<3% body surface area), high-potency topical corticosteroids combined with vitamin D analogues (Calcipotriene) are first-line. For moderate-to-severe disease (≥3-5% BSA or sensitive areas), targeted biologics (anti-IL-23: Risankizumab, Guselkumab; anti-IL-17: Secukinumab, Ixekizumab; anti-TNF: Adalimumab) achieve PASI 90 or PASI 100 skin clearance rates in 70-85% of patients (Phase 3 trials, NEJM/Lancet). Guideline Protocol: Regular daily emollient moisturization; screening for metabolic comorbidities (obesity, hypertension, diabetes) and cardiovascular risk reduction; smoking cessation; screening for psoriatic arthritis. Thresholds: Target: BSA <1% or PASI 90 response at 12-16 weeks.

title: Cellulitis & Purulent Skin Infections: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (IDSA)
snippet: IDSA guidelines classify SSTIs into purulent (abscess, furuncle) and non-purulent (cellulitis, erysipelas). For non-purulent cellulitis, beta-lactam monotherapy covering Streptococcus (Cephalexin or Cefazolin) is recommended (5-day course proven equivalent to 10 days in JAMA RCT). For purulent infections, incision and drainage is the primary therapy; empirical CA-MRSA antibiotic coverage (Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or Doxycycline) is added for systemic signs. Guideline Protocol: Elevation of the affected limb above the level of the heart to promote lymphatic drainage and accelerate resolution; skin demarcation with a pen line to monitor boundary progression; treatment of predisposing factors (e.g., tinea pedis athlete's foot). Thresholds: Hospital admission indicated for systemic toxicity, hemodynamic instability, or failure of oral therapy after 48-72 hours.

title: Clostridioides difficile Infection (CDI): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (IDSA / SHEA)
snippet: Guidelines strongly recommend Fidaxomicin (200 mg BID for 10 days) over oral Vancomycin (125 mg QID for 10 days) as the preferred initial treatment for non-severe and severe CDI (Grade: conditional recommendation), demonstrating superior sustained clinical response and significantly lower recurrence rates. Metronidazole is strongly discouraged. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is recommended for multiple recurrent CDI. Guideline Protocol: Immediate discontinuation of the inciting antibiotic if clinically feasible; strict contact precautions and hand hygiene with soap and water (alcohol sanitizers do not kill C. diff spores); avoid antimotility agents (e.g., Loperamide). Thresholds: Severe CDI defined by WBC ≥15,000 cells/μL or serum creatinine >1.5 mg/dL.

title: Early Localized Lyme Disease: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (IDSA / AAN / ACR)
snippet: Patients with characteristic erythema migrans (EM) rash and history of potential tick exposure in an endemic area should be diagnosed and treated clinically without serologic testing (serology is insensitive in early localized disease, <40%). Oral Doxycycline (100 mg BID for 10-14 days) is first-line treatment. Single-dose prophylactic Doxycycline (200 mg) is recommended within 72 hours of removing an attached Ixodes scapularis tick after ≥36 hours of attachment. Guideline Protocol: Tick prevention education: Insect repellents with DEET or picaridin; wearing permethrin-treated clothing; full-body tick checks within 2 hours of outdoor exposure in wooded/grassy areas; tick removal using fine-tipped tweezers pulling straight up. Thresholds: Two-tiered serological testing (ELISA followed by Western Blot or second enzyme immunoassay) reserved for disseminated disease stages (carditis, facial palsy, arthritis).

title: Colorectal Cancer Screening: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF)
snippet: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years (Grade A). Multiple screening strategies demonstrate strong mortality reduction: Colonoscopy every 10 years, annual Fecal Immunochemical Test (FIT), or stool DNA-FIT (Cologuard) every 3 years. Any positive non-invasive stool test mandates follow-up diagnostic colonoscopy. Guideline Protocol: High dietary fiber intake; regular aerobic exercise; limitation of red and processed meats; smoking cessation and reduction in alcohol intake. Thresholds: Screening begins earlier (age 40 or 10 years before the youngest affected first-degree relative's diagnosis) in individuals with a family history of colorectal cancer.

title: Breast Cancer Screening: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF)
snippet: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years (Grade B). Collaborative modeling indicates that starting screening at age 40 rather than age 50 averts an additional 1.3 breast cancer deaths per 1,000 women screened, with favorable benefit-to-harm ratios regarding false-positive mammograms and benign biopsies. Guideline Protocol: Regular aerobic exercise; weight management post-menopause; limitation of alcohol intake (alcohol is a dose-dependent breast cancer risk factor); breast self-awareness of any changes. Thresholds: Formal hereditary risk assessment (e.g., Tyrer-Cuzick model) and genetic counseling for BRCA1/2 recommended if significant family history of breast/ovarian cancer is present.

title: Lung Cancer Screening: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF & NEJM (NLST))
snippet: The USPSTF recommends annual screening for lung cancer with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years (Grade B). The National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) demonstrated a 20% relative reduction in lung cancer mortality with LDCT compared to chest radiography. Guideline Protocol: Immediate, evidence-based smoking cessation counseling and pharmacotherapy at every screening encounter (smoking cessation reduces lung cancer mortality by >50% over time); radon exposure testing in the home. Thresholds: Lung-RADS structured reporting criteria used to classify pulmonary nodule findings and dictate follow-up intervals.

title: Cervical Cancer Screening & HPV Triage: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF & ASCCP)
snippet: USPSTF recommends screening for cervical cancer in women aged 21 to 65 years. Strategies: Cervical cytology (Pap smear) alone every 3 years for ages 21-29; for ages 30-65, options include high-risk HPV (hrHPV) testing alone every 5 years, hrHPV co-testing with cytology every 5 years, or cytology alone every 3 years. Primary hrHPV testing demonstrates superior sensitivity for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3+ (CIN 3+). Guideline Protocol: HPV vaccination (Gardasil 9) recommended through age 26 (and shared clinical decision-making ages 27-45) to prevent over 90% of HPV-attributable cancers; smoking cessation (smoking impairs cervical clearance of high-risk HPV). Thresholds: ASCCP management guidelines dictate whether a patient requires immediate colposcopy or short-interval 1-year repeat testing based on immediate and 5-year calculated CIN 3+ risk.

title: Crohn's Disease (Inflammatory Bowel Disease): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACG)
snippet: Guidelines recommend a 'Treat-to-Target' strategy aiming for deep mucosal healing, not just symptom resolution. For moderate-to-severe disease, anti-TNF biologics (Infliximab, Adalimumab) or anti-integrins (Vedolizumab) are first-line to induce and maintain remission. Systemic corticosteroids should be used strictly for acute flares and never for maintenance due to severe long-term toxicity. Guideline Protocol: Absolute smoking cessation (smoking doubles the risk of surgical resection and disease recurrence); screening for malnutrition and bone density loss; exclusive enteral nutrition (EEN) in severe pediatric cases. Thresholds: Surgical bowel resection is reserved for medication-refractory disease, strictures causing bowel obstruction, or fistulizing disease.

title: Ulcerative Colitis (Inflammatory Bowel Disease): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACG)
snippet: Unlike Crohn's, UC is limited to the mucosal layer of the colon. For mild-to-moderate UC, topical (rectal) and oral 5-aminosalicylates (5-ASA/Mesalamine) are first-line. For moderate-to-severe disease, targeted biologics (Infliximab, Vedolizumab) or JAK inhibitors (Tofacitinib) are recommended. Annual surveillance colonoscopy is required after 8 years of disease due to significantly elevated colorectal cancer risk. title: Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AHA / ACC)
snippet: Diagnosis is established by a resting Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) ≤0.90. First-line therapy for intermittent claudication is Supervised Exercise Therapy (SET), which increases maximal walking distance by 100-150% (superior to pharmacotherapy). Antiplatelet therapy (Aspirin or Clopidogrel) and high-intensity statin therapy are mandatory to reduce the high risk of myocardial infarction and stroke in PAD patients. Guideline Protocol: Absolute smoking cessation (essential to prevent limb amputation); Supervised Exercise Therapy (treadmill walking to the point of moderate pain, resting, and repeating for 30-45 minutes, 3 times/week); strict foot care and daily inspections. Thresholds: Revascularization (endovascular or surgical bypass) is reserved for lifestyle-limiting claudication unresponsive to SET, or Critical Limb Ischemia (rest pain, non-healing ulcers).

title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (EULAR)
snippet: Hydroxychloroquine is recommended for all patients with SLE, unless contraindicated, as it improves survival, reduces flares, and prevents organ damage (Grade A). Glucocorticoids should be used at the lowest possible dose (target ≤7.5 mg/day of prednisone) and tapered as soon as possible. Belimumab (anti-BAFF) is approved for autoantibody-positive SLE with inadequate response to standard therapy. Guideline Protocol: Strict sun protection (broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF >50, UV-protective clothing) as UV light triggers systemic flares; cardiovascular risk management (SLE carries a significantly elevated risk of premature atherosclerosis); avoidance of sulfa-containing antibiotics. Thresholds: Target: Clinical remission (SLEDAI = 0) or Low Disease Activity (LLDAS) without reliance on chronic systemic steroids.

title: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (CDC)
snippet: Daily oral TDF/FTC (Truvada) or TAF/FTC (Descovy) reduces the risk of getting HIV from sex by about 99% when taken consistently. Long-acting injectable Cabotegravir (Apretude) given every 2 months was shown in HPTN 083/084 trials to be superior to daily oral PrEP in preventing HIV acquisition, offering an option for those with adherence challenges. title: Postmenopausal Bleeding & Endometrial Hyperplasia: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACOG)
snippet: Any postmenopausal bleeding requires immediate investigation to rule out endometrial cancer (present in ~10% of cases). Initial evaluation options are transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) or endometrial biopsy. An endometrial thickness of ≤4 mm on TVUS carries a >99% negative predictive value for endometrial cancer, and observation is reasonable. Thickness >4 mm requires endometrial tissue sampling. Guideline Protocol: Weight management (obesity is a primary risk factor for estrogen-driven endometrial hyperplasia). title: Erectile Dysfunction (ED): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AUA)
snippet: ED is a recognized early clinical marker for underlying Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD); symptoms of ED often precede coronary events by 3-5 years. Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitors (Sildenafil, Tadalafil) are first-line oral therapy. PDE5 inhibitors are absolutely contraindicated in patients taking nitrates (due to severe refractory hypotension) and must be used with caution with alpha-blockers. Guideline Protocol: Cardiovascular risk reduction: strict smoking cessation, weight loss, Mediterranean diet, and aerobic exercise (proven to improve endothelial function and ED severity); psychological counseling for performance anxiety. Thresholds: If oral PDE5 inhibitors fail or are contraindicated, intracavernosal injections (Alprostadil), vacuum erection devices, or surgical penile prostheses are indicated.

title: Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAN)
snippet: First-line evaluation must include checking serum ferritin, as brain iron deficiency is a primary driver of RLS. If ferritin is <75 ng/mL, iron supplementation is the first-line therapy. For pharmacological symptom control, alpha-2-delta ligands (Pregabalin, Gabapentin enacarbil) are preferred. Dopamine agonists (Pramipexole, Ropinirole) are effective but carry a high risk of 'augmentation' (paradoxical worsening of symptoms over time). Guideline Protocol: Avoidance of caffeine, alcohol, and nicotine near bedtime; moderate aerobic exercise; pneumatic compression devices; review of current medications (antidepressants like SSRIs/SNRIs and antihistamines strongly exacerbate RLS). Thresholds: Diagnosis requires URGE criteria: Urge to move legs, Rest worsens symptoms, Getting up/movement relieves symptoms, Evening/nighttime worsening.

title: Acute Appendicitis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (WSES)
snippet: Laparoscopic appendectomy remains the gold standard treatment for acute appendicitis. While non-operative management (antibiotics alone) can be successful in selected patients with uncomplicated appendicitis, there is a recurrence rate of up to 39% at 5 years (CODA trial). Surgery is mandatory for complicated appendicitis (perforation, peritonitis, abscess). Guideline Protocol: Immediate NPO (nothing by mouth) status in the emergency department; IV fluid resuscitation and analgesia. Thresholds: CT scan of the abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast is the most accurate imaging modality in adults; Ultrasound is preferred in children and pregnant women to avoid radiation.

title: Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (KDIGO)
snippet: Severe hyperkalemia (≥6.5 mEq/L) or any hyperkalemia with ECG changes (peaked T waves, widened QRS) is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate myocardial stabilization with IV Calcium Gluconate (or Calcium Chloride). This must be followed by intracellular potassium-shifting agents (IV Insulin with Dextrose, Albuterol) and eventually potassium-removing agents (Loop diuretics, GI cation binders like Patiromer, or emergent Hemodialysis). Guideline Protocol: Strict low-potassium diet restriction; immediate cessation of all potassium-sparing medications (ACEi/ARBs, MRAs like Spironolactone, NSAIDs). Thresholds: Emergent hemodialysis is indicated for hyperkalemia refractory to medical management or in the setting of severe oliguric renal failure.
